question.text: Under Table 3.1 of the SSE framework, the 80G registration under the Income Tax Act is required for NPOs as a mandatory criterion. Which of the following BEST describes the purpose of this 80G disclosure?

answer.text: To enable the entity to disclose whether TAX DEDUCTION is available to investors/donors
To establish that the NPO is GST-registered
To fix the NPO's SEBI listing fee at 50% of standard
To exempt the NPO from SEBI LODR disclosures

explanation.text: The Logic: Table 3.1 states the purpose of the 80G criterion as: 'Entity to ensure disclosure whether tax deduction is available or not to investors.' 80G lets donors claim deduction (50% or 100% of the donation, subject to qualifying limits). SSE requires this to be transparent in the offer document so donors/investors make informed decisions. The Trap: Option A is GST — unrelated. Option C (fee discount) is fiction. Option D (LODR exemption) is wrong — 80G status does not override LODR. Cross-Exam Context: V-A (MF Distributor) tests 80G donor-side (50%/100% split). X-A/X-B (IA) recommend 80G donations for HNI tax planning. XXIII's angle is ISSUER-side disclosure to donors. Assessor's Pro-Tip: When reviewing the 80G disclosure, verify the approval order explicitly states whether the deduction is 50% or 100% and whether the qualifying limit (10% of adjusted GTI) applies. Some NPOs have 100%-without-limit under erstwhile Section 80G(1)(ii) (e.g., PMNRF) — confirm the current status post the 2020 unification regime.
